title: Retirement and Benefits Subscription Services / Request for Information (RFI)
description: DESCRIPTION INTRODUCTION THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) � pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 10 model deviation https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-10, seeking a commercial off-the-shelf web-based, possibly a Software-as-a Service (SaaS), retirement and benefits administration subscription service. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes only. There is no obligation for the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI and any responses to this notice are not offers, and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. The information provided may be used by VBA in developing its acquisition strategy and informing, refining, and finalizing the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their RFI response. Only electronic responses to this RFI will be accepted. The Government will not pay for any time expended or information submitted in response to this RFI. Eligibility in participating in a future acquisition does not depend upon a response to this RFI. BACKGROUND The VBA, Office of Human Capital Services (HCS), is seeking a commercial off-the-shelf web-based, possibly a Software-as-a Service (SaaS), retirement and benefits administration subscription service to provide one comprehensive, centralized repository for VBA employees� health insurance, life insurance, dental & vision insurance, long term care Insurance, Flexible Spending Account, workers compensation benefits, pay and leave retirement services, Thrift Savings Plan (TSP), and Social Security user information. Prior to the use of this subscription service, the HCS Human Resource Centers (HRC) used local Excel tools, which led to inconsistencies and more errors when formulas were changed or corrupted. In addition, several tasks (e.g., Military Service Deposits, complex Service Computation Date (SCD) verifications, creditable time checks, etc.) were difficult or impossible to complete reliably, and there were delays and lack of standardized processes. Retirement and benefits subscription services eliminate these risks, increases visibility into retirement projection, and ensures standardization across HRCs. The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (P.L.118-63) Section 920 allows for the expansion of the BEYOND program. The FAA will implement a BEYOND Phase 2 competitive selection process, through this SIR. This competitive selection process is not a procurement or acquisition under the FAA Acquisition Management System. The FAA did not develop any acquisition requirements for this competitive selection process, and the process will not result in the award of a procurement contract. Consistent with the FAA Administrator�s authorities under 49 U.S.C. �106(l) and (m), this process will result in the award of an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). The FAA intends to award up to eight (8) OTAs through this solicitation. BEYOND Phase 2 has four programmatic focus areas: infrastructure, scalability, safety and automation. Five operational focus areas have also been identified as the greatest challenges that will need to be addressed for progress to be made: public safety, controlled airspace, remote, rural areas with inadequate infrastructure, on-airport operations and cross international borders. This SIR is seeking Offerors who can deliver successful outcomesin support of the BEYOND Phase 2 focus areas. See SIR for details. The FAA intends to competitively award up to eight (8) Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) with SLTTs in accordance with the SIR. The FAA reserves the right to execute additional OTAs if resources permit (49 U.S.C. � 106(l)). The Government will make OTA awards to the Offeror�s determined to best meet the selection criteria which are included in this SIR and reflected in the evaluation of the proposals. Prospective Offerors are encouraged to frequently visit SAM.GOV for any updates to this requirement. description: This project for the Aeronautics Laboratory, is located at the United States Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado. description: Pre-Solicitation Conference � Columbia Class BST-1 Electrical Hull Penetrators and Transmitter Cable Assemblies The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) invites interested contractors to a pre-solicitation conference regarding the future requirement for Columbia Class BST-1 Electrical Hull Penetrators and Transmitter Cable Assemblies. This event is an opportunity for NSWCPD to inform industry partners about this upcoming need and to discuss potential strategies for meeting the demand. What: Pre-Solicitation Conference � � Columbia Class BST-1 Electrical Hull Penetrators and Transmitter Cable Assemblies When: 27 October 2026, 1300 � 1500 Where: Microsoft Teams [Link will be provided to registrants] Why Attend? Learn about NSWCPD's FY27 requirement for Columbia Class BST-1 Electrical Hull Penetrators and Transmitter Cable Assemblies. Understand the scope of the Columbia Class BST-1 Electrical Hull Penetrators and Transmitter Cable Assemblies requirement. Discuss potential acquisition strategies and approaches to meet the anticipated demand for these services. Network with Government representatives to gain a greater insight into our requirements. About the Columbia Class BST-1 Electrical Hull Penetrators and Transmitter Cable Assemblies: The Submarine Sail, Deployed Systems, and Modernization HM&E Engineering (Code 453) and the Undersea Vehicle, Submarine Sail and Deployed Systems Division (Code 45) of the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD), provide support in the development and delivery of systems for Columbia Class New Construction efforts. The projects are for the procurement of Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades construction projects in located at the West Haven VA Medical Center (VAMC) in West Haven, CT, and Togus VAMC, in Togus, ME. Both projects are for design-bid-build phased construction and involve complex electrical and HVAC renovations. VHA PCAC will conduct an industry day to collaborate with general construction contractors and subcontractors of ALL size status� that are interested in doing business with the VA in Connecticut and Maine. The day will start with a meet and greet between VA and Contractor attendees. title: Virtual Industry Engagement: Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan (CERP), Indian River Lagoon South (IRL-S), C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area (C-44 RSTA), Seepage Management Feature - Relief Wells Contract A, Martin County, Florida
description: ADVANCED INDUSTRY DAY ENGAGEMENT - VIRTUAL *** RELATED NOTICE ID: W912EP26Z1BBR *** PROJECT: Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan (CERP), Indian River Lagoon South (IRL-S), C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area (C-44 RSTA), Seepage Management Feature - Relief Wells Contract A, Martin County, Florida 1. PURPOSE OF THIS SPECIAL NOTICE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Jacksonville District, is seeking industry partner feedback in advanced one-on-one engagement sessions regarding the subject project. This is not a typical Industry Day. The purpose of this event is to engage in a two-way dialogue. The Government will share specific project challenges, and we are seeking your information on your capabilities with respect to this project to help enable innovative solutions to be executed within the design plans and specifications. The Government can use these exchanges to learn from industry what is possible to accomplish given current or upcoming advances in technology, best commercial practices, or other approaches to meet Government objectives and accomplish mission needs. 2. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The work is located on approximately 12,000 acres of land in Martin County, Florida directly north of Citrus Boulevard and the C-44 Canal (also known as the St. Lucie Canal), halfway between Lake Okeechobee and the Atlantic Ocean. For purposes of this construction contract, the anticipated location of site activities will occur throughout the current C-44 Reservoir site adjacent to the perimeter canal. The work consists of constructing groundwater pressure relief wells adjacent to the C-44 reservoir embankment. The work generally consists of: Construction of approximately 126 fully designed relief wells at prescribed locations. Construction of well outfall system consisting of a precast manhole, pipe and discharge end section for each relief well to drain into the adjacent canal. Documenting the construction, development, and pump testing of all wells. Well construction will require managing borehole wall stability for a variety of subsurface conditions that may consist of surficial clayey and silty sands, very loose uniform fine sands, dense sands having varying degrees of cementation, limestone/sandstone, and sand to cobble size shells. Groundwater conditions are likely to be artesian at the well locations. Specific Project Challenges: The work includes construction of wells at approximately 60 ft deep. The relief well will have a 10-inch diameter stainless steel riser and high flow screen, constructed in an 18 to 24-inch diameter borehole. The anulus between the borehole and riser will be backfilled with a uniform and non-calcareous filter media commonly used in the water well industry and selected for compatibility with the encountered subsurface materials. Well construction will require managing borehole wall stability for a variety of subsurface conditions that may consist of surficial clayey and silty sands, very loose uniform fine sands, dense sands having varying degrees of cementation, limestone/sandstone, and sand to cobble size shells. Groundwater conditions are likely to be artesian at the well locations. Above the screen and filter media, the borehole will be sealed with bentonite and grout. All backfill materials will be placed by tremie method. The existing canal is approximately 35 feet from the well locations. The groundwater level varies with reservoir stage and can be expected to be higher than the canal water level. The canal water level varies (normally approximately EL 18.5 ft) and can increase up to 2 ft above normal stage during project operations. The reservoir pool varies and can be expected to be between EL 29.0 ft and EL 36 ft (3 ft to 10 ft pool) during the period of performance. The Target Price range is between $25,000,000 and $50,000,000. The goal period of performance for this project is 24-30 months from receipt of Notice to Proceed (NTP), including options for a subset of the wells. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard for this project is $45.0 million. 3. DISCUSSION TOPICS Attached to this notice are the draft plans and specifications. We ask you to review these documents and come prepared to discuss your observations and insights in the following areas: Design & Construction Aspects of the current design that limit speed of construction, add cost without apparent need or improvement in quality or function, preclude more efficient means/methods/equipment. Ambiguities, apparent errors, missing information or other aspects in the plans and specifications that are unclear. Optimizations in regard to the drilling and well construction specifications related to equipment, borehole stability, installation and development. Aspects of the design that present constructability challenges. Critical factors in the design that would inhibit a reduced period of performance. Schedule & Logistics Optimal sequencing strategies to minimize the overall period of performance, and whether the draft specifications provide sufficient flexibility to execute those sequences. Long-lead materials or equipment that the Government should consider procuring now to advance the schedule. Identification of Government actions, administrative decisions, information, or reviews (e.g., submittal approvals) that must be available early in the process to support an optimized schedule. Other Topics: Impact of inclusion of a Project Labor Agreement (PLA). Interest in submitting a proposal for this project. Your firm�s bonding capability for this size of project. 4. ENGAGEMENT FORMAT: VIRTUAL ONE-ON-ONE SESSIONS The Government will be holding confidential, one-hour one-on-one virtual sessions. This format is designed to protect your proprietary ideas and allow for a substantive engagement in the most important aspects listed above. In accordance with RFO 15.101(d), when information about a proposed acquisition is disclosed to one or more potential offerors and that information is necessary for the preparation of proposals, the information should be made available to the public as soon as practicable in order to avoid creating an unfair competitive advantage. 5. EVENT INFORMATION / REGISTRATION Date: October 29 & 30, 2026 Time: To be established upon registration Interested firms who consider themselves qualified to perform this project and would like to participate, a session request must be sent. One-hour slots will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. To request a session, please email Manuela D. Voicu at manuela.d.voicu@usace.army.mil and Martha G. Sequeira at martha.g.sequeira@usace.army.mil no later than 1600 ET October 23, 2026, indicating your preferred date and one hour block (0900�1200 or 1300�1600). The Government will issue an email confirming your time and meeting invite. 6. WHO SHOULD ATTEND All interested Prime Contractors and potential Joint Ventures are invited to attend. 7. DISCLAIMER This is NOT a solicitation. This announcement is for planning and market research purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government. Participation in this event is voluntary and at no cost to the Government. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with participation. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of the information received at this event or otherwise pay for the information requested. Information received from Industry will be treated as information only and not as a proposal.

title: FY27 USAFA Cader Swimsuits and Compression Shorts
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FY27 USAFA CADET SWIMSUITS AND COMPRESSION SHORTS (REQUIREMENTS CONTRACT) THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION; THIS NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing the information provided to the Government. The United States Air Force Academy (USAFA), 10th Logistics Readiness Squadron Cadet Uniform Section (10 LRS/LGRCU), has a recurring, mandatory-issue requirement to outfit cadets with athletic swimsuits and compression shorts. Garments are mandatory-issue items used for physical education, athletic training, and scheduled cadet clothing issue events, with a delivery due date each April. The Government intends to solicit and award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Requirements Contract in accordance with FAR 16.503, consisting of one (1) 12-month base period and four (4) consecutive 12-month option periods. The following estimated quantities represent projected annual requirements (exact quantities and sizes will be included with the award): 0001 Shorts Compression MNS 2,850 each 0002 Shorts Compression WMNS 450 each 0003 Swimsuit MNS 500 each 0004 Swimsuit WMNS 170 each SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS / SPECIFICATIONS Garments proposed must meet or exceed the following salient characteristics: A. Cadet Compression Shorts (Men�s & Women�s) Fabric & Material: Form-fitting nylon/elastane-type fabric blend; 4-way stretch elastic performance construction. Moisture Management: Advanced moisture-wicking material engineered to pull sweat away from the skin, lessening chafing and rash onset during rigorous athletic training. Athletic Performance: Form-fitting garment providing compression to keep thigh muscles warm and reduce muscle fatigue/strain; incorporates athletic performance standards comparable to NFL Combine compression gear. Color: Dark Navy Blue throughout (uniform dyed fabric through and through). Coverage & Inseam: Men�s: Mid-thigh coverage with standard athletic compression inseam. Women�s: Specifically tailored female cut with a shorter inseam of 2" to 4". B. Cadet Men�s Swimsuit Shell Material: 100% Polyester Taslan. Liner: Synthetic mesh brief liner (anti-chafing construction). Waistband: Elastic waistband equipped with an internal or external drawstring / drawcord. Inseam: 5" to 8" inseam length. Construction: Lightweight, quick-drying, durable, and anti-chafing. Color: Royal Blue. Standard Sizing Breakdown: X-Small (XSM): 24"�27" waist Small (SM): 28"�31" waist Medium (MED): 32"�35" waist Large (LG): 36"�39" waist Extra Large (XLG): 40"�44" waist Double Extra Large (XXLG): 45"�47" waist C. Cadet Women�s Swimsuit Fabric Composition: 85% Polyester / 15% Elastane (Poly/Elastane 85/15 blend). Design & Cut: Athletic one-piece suit with moderate/standard leg cut and wide support straps. Back Style: Performance / Racerback styling with keyhole opening. Support & Lining: Built-in shelf bra; fully lined front and back. Color: Royal Blue. Standard Sizing Breakdown: Size 30 / XXSM (Dress size 00�0) Size 32 / XSM (Dress size 0�2) Size 34 / SM (Dress size 4�6) Size 36 / MED (Dress size 8�10) Size 38 / LG (Dress size 12�14) Size 40 / XLG (Dress size 16�18) Size 42 / XXLG (Dress size 20�22) Government-Furnished Material (GFM): No Government Furnished Material or Property will be provided. The contractor is entirely responsible for sourcing and procuring all fabric, trims, threads, and packaging. Domestic Preference / Sourcing: The Buy American Act and applicable Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) clauses (e.g., DFARS 252.225-7001 / Berry Amendment DFARS 252.225-7012 as applicable to military apparel acquisitions) will apply. First Article Testing (FAT): A First Article Sample will be required upon contract award prior to mass production in accordance with FAR 52.209-4 (First Article Approval - Government Testing) or Alternate I. Delivery Terms: FOB Destination to USAFA Cadet Uniform Section (10 LRS/LGRCU), 2348 Sijan Hall, USAF Academy, CO 80840. In response to this sources sought provide the following capabilities package: Company Profile Company Information: Legal Business Name, physical address, point of contact (name, email, phone number), and website. Identification Identifiers: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE Code, and SAM.gov registration status (must be active with no exclusions). Business Size & Socio-Economic Classifications: Confirm whether your firm is a Small Business under NAICS 315250 (750 employees) and specify any certified socio-economic designations (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB/EDWOSB, SDVOSB, Small Disadvantaged Business). Technical & Manufacturing Capability Scope Coverage: Indicate whether your firm can manufacture and supply both product categories (Swimsuits AND Compression Shorts) or only a specific subset. Multi-Year Capacity: Demonstrate your company�s production and supply chain capacity to support an ongoing Requirements Contract over a 5-year period (Base plus 4 Option Years) meeting the estimated annual quantities and sizing distributions. Domestic Sourcing Compliance: State your ability to comply with domestic sourcing requirements (Buy American Act / Berry Amendment DFARS requirements) and manufacturing origin. Lead Times: Typical lead time required for First Article Sample submission and subsequent standard production order turnaround times. Please note: All contractors doing business with the Federal Government must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. The website for registration is www.sam.gov. Responses must be submitted electronically via email to the following points of contact: Primary Point of Contact: Melinda Lingley - melinda.lingley@us.af.mil Secondary Point of Contact: Wanda Farr - wanda.farr@us.af.mil Response Due Date: Responses are due no later than 23 October 2026 at 2:00 PM MST. Interested vendors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for updates.

title: RFI For Army Acquisition Talent Management Solution (AATMS)
description: The current CAMP/CAPPMIS environment cannot rapidly assimilate evolving acquisition workforce credentialing frameworks, credential updates, or statutorily mandated policy revisions. Disparate record silos degrade data integrity and deny leadership real-time visibility into workforce readiness. The Army seeks a commercial, outcomes-focused capability that consolidates acquisition talent functions into an authoritative user hub. The objective is to replace disparate legacy modules with an adaptable, commercially available platform that automates and simplifies workflows, protects and secures workforce information, synchronizes with Army enterprise repositories, and delivers role-tailored dashboards and analytics for leaders, career managers, supervisors, and workforce members. *This Draft RFI has been extended to Friday October 23, 2026 at 16:00 PST.

title: FA2204_RFI_TACMOR_System
description: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Strategic Sensors Branch (AFLCMC/ESGS) is conducting market research to identify qualified systems integrators capable of designing, developing, producing, installing, operating, and sustaining the full lifecycle of the Tactical Multi-Mission Over-the-Horizon Radar (TACMOR) system. TACMOR is a Middle Tier of Acquisition (MTA) Rapid Prototyping initiative intended to field an operational, remotely operated Over-the-Horizon Radar (OTHR) capability within the Indo-Pacific region. The system will deliver wide-area air domain awareness and support supplementary operational missions across the United States Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM) Area of Responsibility (AOR). The anticipated contract award is slated for FY2027, with an estimated period of performance extending through FY2029. The TACMOR baseline system architecture requires a bistatic operational profile featuring geographically separated transmit (Tx) and receive (Rx) installations deployed in austere operational environments within the designated operational area. The system will operate as a one-dimensional, remotely operated OTHR integrating permanent antenna field installations with modular, containerized mission support facilities. Comprehensive integrator solutions must address primary and backup self-sustained onsite power generation and fuel storage, physical and electronic security, remote health and status monitoring, secure backhaul communications, environmental resilience against tropical and saltwater conditions, and integration with a centralized Radar Operations Control Center (ROCC). The Government will furnish land, Military Construction (MILCON), and the prepared receive and transmit sites. The Government may also provide black transport communications via fiber optic networks with satellite communications (SATCOM) backup; complete cryptographic and backhaul transport parameters are detailed in the CUI technical data package. Respondents must demonstrate mature technical approaches, industrial base capacity, software engineering maturity, and specialized workforce availability to achieve full integration and system sell-off by 30 September 2029.

description: The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualifications to support repairability maintainability, and sustaining engineering for the modified WC-130J RTP APN-241 Weather Radar. Potential sources must possess the ability to provide engineering studies for the WC-130J RTP APN-241 system in resolving reliability and maintainability issues, obsolete parts issues, identify and propose solutions to Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) issues, and analyze failure trends from both the depots and the field level shops to support the MC-130J CR-2M developmental testing. For vendors wishing to participate in this Request for Information (RFI), after reviewing the requirement, provide documentation supporting proof of company�s capability to meet the requested requirements. If lacking sufficient experience/capabilities in a particular area, please provide details explaining strategies to overcome the lack of experience/capabilities to perform that portion of the requirement. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c), this RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or services. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses incurred in response to this RFI; all cost associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in future RFPs nor does it ensure participation, if an RFP is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Federal Business Opportunities (SAM.gov) website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Potential sources must be able to install the APN-241 Weather radar in addition to troubleshooting system discrepancies. Potential sources must be capable of and have access to Northrop Grumman equipment. Potential sources would need to have the ability to ensure equipment would be able to detect rain rates in real-time directly in front of the aircraft either proving or disproving the capability. The proposed services are required to have access to Northrop Grumman Corporation, and their databases which contain/maintain the APN-241 Radar System engineering software. The following equipment is required to sustain WC-130J RTP and will be provided as GFE: RTP P/N 780R270G10 (NSN 5841-01-522-1618), Transmitter Module (1A05) P/N 444R372G01 (NSN 5841-01-433-9455), and General-Purpose Processor Module P/N 824R061G06 (NSN 5998-01-534-5169). The modified configuration provided is the following equipment: WC-130J RTP P/N 780R270G13 (NSN 5841-01-546-5654), Transmitter Module (1A05) P/N 444R372G02 (NSN 6130-01-433-9452). And General- Purpose Processor Module P/N 824R061G13 (NSN 5998-01-564-1569). Provide sustaining engineering support and repairment of the modified configuration: WC-130J RTP P/N 780R270G13 (NSN 5841-01-546-5654), Transmitter Module (1A05) P/N 444R372G02 (NSN 6130-01-433-9452), and General-Purpose Processor Module P/N 824R061G13 (NSN 5998-01-564-1569) Provide engineering support during developmental testing not to exceed 400-man hours and provide on-site support at Eglin AFB for two engineers for a total of three 5-day trips. title: Building 510 Substation Upgrade - Phase I
description: Notice of Interest: BSA is seeking interested contractors capable of performing the work describled below and interested in receiving the forthcoming solicitation. The formal solicitation will be issued at a later date and will also be posted on SAM.gov at that time. Note that switchgear and transformers are being provided to the contractor as Government Furnished Equipment (GFE). Interested contractors are invited to submit a statement of interest along with a capabilities statement to BSA's Contract Specialist, Megan Howard, at mhoward@bnl.gov. Please include your Sam.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Project Description: The Physics Building was constructed in 1962 and much of the electrical system, original to the building, is beyond its useful life. These systems are also not compliant with current building codes, contain hazardous materials and need complete upgrades. The existing protective devices may not operate as specified, increasing the potential for arc-flash hazards and system damaging electrical faults. Repairs are cost prohibitive and may lead to extended unplanned outages in this mission critical facility. The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials (except as noted below), equipment, and services necessary for complete removal and upgrading of the existing Building 510 electrical substation equipment that feeds the newly replaced electrical distribution switchgear. This project includes the removal of two medium voltage substation transformers, one medium voltage oil switch and medium voltage distribution cabling. The project also includes the installation of a new exterior substation with two new medium voltage transformers, one pad mounted medium voltage switchgear and medium voltage feeders in a new concrete encased duct bank. The new substation will be constructed in the north-loading dock parking lot, complete with new transformer and switchgear pads, grounding and crushed stone. Long lead electrical equipment procurements are planned early in the project and construction of the substation infrastructure can be completed in parallel. Once the cutovers are completed the old transformers and oil switch will be removed from the equipment vault in the basement of Building 510. The Contractor shall not procure the switchgear or transformers under this contract. Installation will be executed in a phased approach in order to minimize electric service disruptions to the building and will provide provisions for future redundant circuit configuration.

The United States Air Force Academy (USAFA), 10th Logistics Readiness Squadron Cadet Uniform Section (10 LRS/LGRCU), has a recurring, mandatory-issue requirement to outfit cadets with athletic swimsuits and compression shorts. Garments are mandatory-issue items used for physical education, athletic training, and scheduled cadet clothing issue events, with a delivery due date each April. Cadet Compression Shorts (Men�s & Women�s) Fabric & Material: Form-fitting nylon/elastane-type fabric blend; 4-way stretch elastic performance construction. Moisture Management: Advanced moisture-wicking material engineered to pull sweat away from the skin, lessening chafing and rash onset during rigorous athletic training. Athletic Performance: Form-fitting garment providing compression to keep thigh muscles warm and reduce muscle fatigue/strain; incorporates athletic performance standards comparable to NFL Combine compression gear. Color: Dark Navy Blue throughout (uniform dyed fabric through and through). Coverage & Inseam: Men�s: Mid-thigh coverage with standard athletic compression inseam. Women�s: Specifically tailored female cut with a shorter inseam of 2" to 4". B. Cadet Men�s Swimsuit Shell Material: 100% Polyester Taslan. Liner: Synthetic mesh brief liner (anti-chafing construction). Waistband: Elastic waistband equipped with an internal or external drawstring / drawcord. Inseam: 5" to 8" inseam length. Construction: Lightweight, quick-drying, durable, and anti-chafing. Color: Royal Blue. Cadet Women�s Swimsuit Fabric Composition: 85% Polyester / 15% Elastane (Poly/Elastane 85/15 blend). Design & Cut: Athletic one-piece suit with moderate/standard leg cut and wide support straps. Back Style: Performance / Racerback styling with keyhole opening. Support & Lining: Built-in shelf bra; fully lined front and back. Color: Royal Blue. Standard Sizing Breakdown: Size 30 / XXSM (Dress size 00�0) Size 32 / XSM (Dress size 0�2) Size 34 / SM (Dress size 4�6) Size 36 / MED (Dress size 8�10) Size 38 / LG (Dress size 12�14) Size 40 / XLG (Dress size 16�18) Size 42 / XXLG (Dress size 20�22) Government-Furnished Material (GFM): No Government Furnished Material or Property will be provided. title: INDUSTRY DAYS - WEST HAVEN, CT & TOGUS, ME
description: ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD MODERNIZATION CONSTRUCTION OPPORTUNITIES The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) is hosting an industry day and is seeking information and potential sources to determine a set-aside, if any, is appropriate for two projects located in the New England area valued between $40M and $100M. The projects are for the procurement of Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades construction projects in located at the West Haven VA Medical Center (VAMC) in West Haven, CT, and Togus VAMC, in Togus, ME. Both projects are for design-bid-build phased construction and involve complex electrical and HVAC renovations. VHA PCAC will conduct an industry day to collaborate with general construction contractors and subcontractors of ALL size status� that are interested in doing business with the VA in Connecticut and Maine. The day will start with a meet and greet between VA and Contractor attendees. We will review the design drawings and specifications, conduct a high-level site walkthrough, and discuss the phasing of the project. This will ensure all interested contractors understand the intent and requirements for the project. This industry day will help the VA determine the method of procurement, such as tradeoff, and type of socioeconomic set-aside, if any, highlight any industry concerns, gauge general contractor interest in the project, and perform a site walk to show key areas of the project. This is an opportunity for industry to influence procurement decisions that will shape the course of the project. Your feedback and collaboration is vital for successful construction and deployment of the EHR program. PROJECT DESCRIPTION / DESCRIPTION OF WORK / REQUIREMENT The VA is seeking general contractors to furnish all labor, materials, equipment, and supervision, and perform all work necessary to prepare the site for building operations and complete the EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades construction projects at VA Medical Centers in West Haven, CT, and Togus, ME. Work includes general construction, alterations, telecommunications, electrical, HVAC, Plumbing, Hazardous Waste Removal, and other disciplines as required to complete the scope of these projects. Projects involve expansion of existing telecommunication rooms (TRs), power upgrades, replacement of data cabling with CAT6A, renovation of existing data center to include power / data / equipment / HVAC. All work is to be performed in accordance with the drawings and specifications. ADMINISTRATIVE The industry day will be held on October 27, 2026 in Togus, ME and October 28, 2026 in West Haven, CT from 9:00 AM ET to 12:00 PM ET at each location. The meeting location for Togus will be the auditorium in Building 210 at the Togus campus located at 810 Eastern Avenue, Augusta ME 04330. The meeting location for West Haven will be the Donaldson Center in Building 2 at the West Haven campus located at 950 Campbell Avenue, West Haven, CT 06516. Take the elevator to the second floor and follow signs to Donaldson Center �C�. title: Q522--On-site Board-Certified/Board-Eligible Diagnostic Radiology Physician Services | Orlando VA Healthcare System (OVAHCS)
description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 4 of 4 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 4 The Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 08, Orlando VA Healthcare System (OVAHCS), 13800 Veteran s Way, Orlando, FL 32827, intends to solicit an unrestricted full and open competitive Request for Proposals (RFP), to provide services necessary to perform two (2) Full Time Employee Equivalent (FTEE) on-site Board-Certified/Board-Eligible Diagnostic Radiology Physician Services (body imaging, Muscoskeletal (MSK) or Neuroradiology qualified) to eligible beneficiaries of the OVAHCS. The VA Radiology Services follow the standards & guidelines set forth by American College of Radiology (ACR). A contractor providing Diagnostic Radiology Physician Services shall provide services that meet or exceed the American College of Radiology Guidelines https://www.acr.org/-/media/ACR/Files/Practice-Parameters/IRClin-Prac-Mgmt.pdf.pdf. Two (2) Diagnostic Radiologists of differing subspecialties (one (1) Neuro and one (1) MSK; (1) Neuro and one (1) body; or one (1) MSK and one (1) body) are required to be onsite Monday Friday from 8:00am 4:30pm (30-minute lunch) excluding Federal Holidays (full-time basis). No off-hours coverage, on-call duties, or overtime are required. Each Diagnostic Radiologists must produce 9000 work Relative Value Units (wRVUs)/year (4.3 wRVUs/hour; 34.6 wRVUs/day). Qualified substitute personnel with credentials including board-certification/board-eligibility, comparable to designated key personnel must be fully credentialed and privileged and readily available to provide services in the event key personnel are unavailable. Given the importance of continuity of care to the Facility s medical services, the Contractor must maintain a contingency plan to ensure uninterrupted services if a physician departs employment or becomes unable to perform services and provide coverage. Contractor physicians must possess a minimum of three (3) years of continuous Board-Certified/Board-Eligible Diagnostic Radiologist experience within the last four (4) years, including demonstrated proficiency in interpreting Computed Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Ultrasound, and Diagnostic X-ray imaging. QUALIFICATIONS: License: The Contractor s physician(s) assigned by the Contractor to perform the services covered by this contract shall have a current license to practice medicine in any State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States or the District of Columbia) when services are performed onsite on VA property. All licenses held by the key personnel working on this contract shall be full and unrestricted licenses. Contractor s physician(s) who have current, full and unrestricted licenses in one or more states, but who have, or ever had, a license restricted, suspended, revoked, voluntarily revoked, voluntarily surrendered pending action or denied upon application will not be considered for the purposes of this contract. Board Certification: All contractor s physician(s) shall be Board-Certified /Board-Eligible per the American Board of Radiology (http://www.theabr.org/). All continuing education courses required for maintaining certification must be kept up to date at all times. Documentation verifying current certification shall be provided by the Contractor to the VA COR on an annual basis for each year of contract performance. Credentialing and Privileging: Credentialing and privileging is to be done in accordance with the provisions of VHA Directive 1100.20 and VHA Directive 1100.21 referenced above. The Contractor is responsible for ensuring that proposed physician(s) possesses the requisite credentials enabling the granting of privileges. No services shall be provided by any Contractor s physician(s) prior to obtaining approval by the Facility Medical Executive Board and Medical Center Director. The period of performance is expected to be from February 1, 2027, through January 31, 2032. The authority of for this procurement is Title 38 USC 8153, Health Care Resources (HCR) Sharing Authority, Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, and RFO 15, Contracting by Negotiation. The solicitation document will be issued as Request for Proposals (RFP) 36C24827R0006 as an unrestricted open and competitive solicitation on or about November 2, 2026. Interested contractors will be responsible for downloading copies of the solicitation and any subsequent amendments from this website. No hard copies will be made available. The solicitation will provide instructions to contractors about the response to the RFP submission process. Prospective contractors are encouraged to register their interest in the solicitation on the SAM.gov | Contract Opportunities website so that they are notified of the issuance of the solicitation and any amendments. In accordance with RFO 52.204-7, System for Award Management (SAM), prospective contractors must be registered in SAM to be eligible for award. Contractors may obtain SAM information at https://sam.gov/. Registration is free and potential offerors are encouraged to visit the SAM website (SAM.gov | Entity Information). The NAICS Code for this procurement is 621111 Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists); Product/Service Code: Q522 Medical-Radiology. The Business Size Standard is $16 million. Any questions concerning this announcement should be directed to Jayne Messer, Contracting Officer, via electronic mail (email) at jayne.messer@va.gov and include the solicitation number on subject line (i.e., RFP 36C24827R0006).

Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. Repaired Government equipment shall meet the inspection and acceptance test requirements of the applicable repair specifications. A contractor QA representative shall be required, in accordance with MIL-I-45208A, or ISO Quality standard equivalent, to witness repair,inspection, and acceptance tests Government representatives shall be notified of, and permitted to witnesssuch inspections at their discretion. The contractor shall submit repair procedures for Government approval prior to repair if those procedures deviate from the repair procedures detailed in the applicable repair specifications. Where the test specifications are found to be missing,inadequate,or behind in revision for a CLIN,the contractor shall develop and submit its own acceptance test procedures for Government approval to submission of the CLIN for Government acceptance. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. The Variable Inlet Ramp (Diffuser) is used to control airflow to assist with engine performance. It is designed solely for F-15 applications and used on F-15 E and EX model aircraft only. Impediment to Competition: The original equipment manufacturer for this item is The Boeing Company (Support Equipment Systems and Services), CAGE 76301. The Government does not own any data, drawings, schematics, or any other releasable technical data in support of this requirement. As a result, the Boeing Company is the only known source with adequate knowledge of the performance requirements and possession of the required technical data and capabilities needed to produce this item and ensure compatibility of the equipment. INTEREST: The DLA/AWB Contracting Office intends to award a sole source contract to The Boeing Company for the Manufacture of the F-15 Variable Inlet Ramp (Left Hand) in support of the F-15 E model aircraft. Other interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement no later than 23 October 2026 by emailing roberto.martinez-perez@dla.mil and amy.hatfield@us.af.mil. The Government intends to procure these items using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. DISCLAIMER: This Source Sought Synopsis is for informational purposes only. This is not a request for proposal. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers, and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract because of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents to this technical description is strictly voluntary.

Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. title: Maintenance, Repair and Preservation of YT-811
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YT-811. The YT-811 characteristics are Length: 90 FT, Width: 38FT 5IN, Age: 4 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 16 FT, Full Displacement: 494 L Tons and Light Load: 438 L Tons.The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YT-811 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. The Government will transport the vessel to the Contractors repair facility. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Replace zinc anodes. Blast and preserve underwater hull and freeboard, bulwarks, and handrails. Blast and preserve main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck non-skid, FME all polished stainless steel surfaces. Perform hull and freeboard Ultrasonic Test (UT) inspections. Perform hull and freeboard, main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck Visual Inspections (VT). Repair hull and winch valves. Repair deckhouse expansion joint. Test and preserve CHT, ballast, potable water, fuel oil, waste oil and day tanks. Accomplish Mast Lighting and Deckhouse Lighting Repairs. Replace all placards and labels on main, 1st and 2nd decks. Replace deck winch, mast, and brow systems hydraulic hoses. Accomplish winch control piping modification (YT-0104D). Overhaul Mast hydraulic ram, replace pins and bushings. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Upon completion of all work the Government will take custody of the vessel. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by this Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in section 3.0 of this Statement of Work.The YT-811 will be ready for pick up on or after 2 March 2027. Refer to page 1 Request for Quote (RFQ) of the Solicitation regarding desired and required delivery information.This is full and open competition. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov.

title: Market Intelligence Notice � Hangar Construction (Hybrid Conventional and Tension Fabric Structures)
description: Market Intelligence Notice � Hangar Construction (Hybrid Conventional and Tension Fabric Structures) Disclaimer: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a commitment to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. 1.0 Objective The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Savannah District (SAS) is seeking market intelligence to identify and assess industry capabilities relevant to Tension Fabric Structures (TFS) and hybrid industrialized construction solutions for hangar facilities and similar large-span mission support applications. The Government is pursuing modern industrialized construction approaches intended to improve schedule, cost, and lifecycle outcomes for this facility type. Information provided by respondents will be used to help the Government understand available market participants, solution types, and industry interest, and will inform future industry engagements, acquisition planning, and assessment of potential use of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, Facility Construction or Repair: Transactions Other Than Contracts and Grants. 2.0 Forecasted Projects - Overview The following projects are currently projected for potential TFS or hybrid industrialized construction applications. USACE, SAS requires a highly resilient, energy-efficient operational hangar facility that can be rapidly constructed, scaled, and reconfigured as a tension-fabric structure. Solutions may be scaled for additional hangar facilities identified later. Maintenance Hangar, Hunter Army Airfield (HAAF), GA (approximately 193,513 square footage (SF)). Construction of a Large (10 Module) Standard Design Aircraft Maintenance Hangar Complex with integrated aviation maintenance operations, maintenance support, company operations, flight planning, flight operations spaces, Ground Support Equipment (GSE) covered storage, Associated Support Items of Equipment (ASIOE) covered storage, Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) and Hazardous Material (HAZMAT) storage, hangar access and wash aprons. Project also includes fire protection and alarm systems, information systems, Intrusion Detection System (IDS) installation, closed circuit television connection, cybersecurity measures, and Energy Monitoring Control Systems (EMCS) connection. Supporting facilities include site development, utilities and connections, exterior lighting, paving, POV parking, walks, storm drainage, information systems, landscaping and signage. Heating and air conditioning will be provided by self-contained system. Moody Air Force Base, GA (approximately 105,000 SF). Construction of an adequately sized six-bay hangar and squadron operations facility. The squadron operations section of the facility shall incorporate mission planning, life support, and squadron admin space. The aircraft maintenance section shall be designed to optimize maintenance administration for the squadron. The hangar bays will provide space to support aircraft repair and inspection, engine changes, and other activities that must be accomplished in a secure, climate-controlled environment. The hangar space must be sized to accommodate movement and placement of maintenance equipment around the aircraft and systems supporting the aircraft. 3.0 Requested Information & Market Intelligence Questionnaire Section - General Information Provide responses to the survey linked herein. https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/8B5GPKqrMh Section - Capabilities Respondents are asked to structure Capability Statements to include the following elements: Corporate Overview - A brief summary of your firm's core capabilities, relevant experience, and capacity to perform the type of work contemplated under this RFI. Commercial Best Practices. To the extent available, provide information regarding commercial best practices applicable to the contemplated construction delivery method, including: Typical pricing/payment structures Geographic coverage Typical project schedule timelines, long lead items, and key decision points Key considerations and risk associated with permitting, logistics, staffing/labor availability, and construction execution. Specialized Systems Integration: Describe your experience integrating specialized hangar systems, such as high-capacity cranes, fall protection systems, and high-expansion foam fire suppression systems, within a tension fabric structure. Supply Chain and Logistics: Describe your supply chain for key components of the tension fabric structure. What are your typical lead times for material and fabrication? Materials and Durability: What specific materials, coatings, and structural frame materials do you typically use for facilities of this type and in a coastal environment? What is the expected design life and warranty period for these components? 3. Survey Responses � Please provide detailed responses to Survey Questions 10 through 12 (listed below and on the survey form). Respondents are asked to integrate these responses directly into their capability statements; separate or stand-alone survey responses are not required. Additional Information � Respondents may include other information that demonstrates their relevant capabilities, experience, and capacity. Examples include: Photos of TFS projects ; Smart Building Technologies (e.g., automated controls, sensors, energy management systems, fire protection and alarm systems, information systems, Intrusion Detection System (IDS) installation, closed circuit television connection, cybersecurity measures, and Energy Monitoring Control Systems (EMCS) connection.) Advanced HVAC Systems (e.g., high-efficiency climate control, specialized filtration) Survey Questions 10-12 10. Describe your experience or capability in designing and constructing tension-fabric structures that could innovate and accelerate construction. 11. Describe your firm�s practical experience with collaborative delivery models, such as Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build or Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), where your team was integrated into the design phase. What specific pre-construction services did you provide? 12. For the projects listed in response to Q11, identify the major subcontractor(s) used and describe their qualifications. Detail the teaming relationship and contract structure between the construction contractor, the owner, and the Designer of Record. Explain how your team's involvement improved the final design quality, accelerated the delivery schedule, and reduced overall project cost. 4.0 Response Submission Instructions Format: Responses to the survey must be submitted via the link provided. The capability statement must be submitted in PDF format, single-spaced, using 11-point font or larger. Submission Deadline: October 23, 2026 � 5:00 PM Submission Channel: Complete the survey at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/8B5GPKqrMh Submit capability statement via email to the Agreement Officer (AO) at Jennifer.L.Murphy@usace.army.mil and copy Sabrina.Bastine@usace.army.mil with the subject line: "USACE OTA Market Intelligence Response TFS - [Company Name]". Proprietary Information: Any proprietary, sensitive, or business-confidential information must be clearly marked as such on each page to ensure proper handling by USACE SAS.

title: HPCMP Innovative Technology Insertion of Advanced HPC Systems Commercial Solutions Openings (CSO)
description: The Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) is issuing a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) pursuant to DFARS Subpart 212.70. Under a CSO, the ERDC may competitively award proposals received in response to a general solicitation, similar to a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), to acquire innovative commercial products, technologies, or services based on a review of solutions by scientific, technological, or other subject matter expert peers within the ERDC. �Innovative,� for CSO purposes, means any new technology, process, or method, including research and development (R&D), or any new application of an existing technology, process, or method. Under this CSO, all products, technologies, and services shall be treated as commercial items; products, technologies, and services do not have to be �commercially available� to be submitted in response to this solicitation. If the solution meets the requirements of the regulation, the solution is treated as commercial whereby the Contracting Officer will utilize commercial procedures to develop and execute the resultant award. The DoW High Performance Computing Modernization Program (HPCMP) is seeking innovative solutions to establish a new high-performance computing (HPC) system acquisition and support services model that leverages industry best practices to transform how the HPCMP procures, operates, and maintains its newest HPC systems for 2027. The HPC systems being considered are a combination of compute-intensive architectures and artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) platforms operating in either unclassified or classified (secret and above-secret) environments. The systems would be geographically distributed at up to three of the five HPCMP DoW Supercomputing Resource Centers (DSRCs). Since the systems will reside on-premises in the DSRCs, the services model must also conform to DoW and local Service policies, especially regarding security (physical, personnel, and cyber). To navigate the current market conditions and meet mission objectives, a new strategy is needed to design, manufacture, deliver, install, operate and maintain one or more HPC systems at one to three different HPC centers. The anticipated systems will be a combination of compute-intensive architectures (mostly CPU-based) and artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) platforms (mostly GPU-based) operating in either unclassified or classified (secret and above-secret) environments. Go to https://www.erdcwerx.org/innovative-technology-insertion-of-advanced-hpc-systems/ for all of the CSO details and submission requirements. All solutions must be submitted through the ERDCWERX platform. The ERDC may award a FAR-based contract or an Other Transaction under this announcement. All resultant FAR-based contracts will be firm-fixed price. All items, technologies, and services (including research and development) procured via this CSO are treated as commercial. Applicants from universities and/or non-profit organizations should be aware that commercial clauses will be integrated into the award and should coordinate proposals with associated legal counsel prior to submission.

title: Request for Information: United States Coast Guard Core Navigation Software
description: Description & Purpose of Request 1.1 Objective The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 to identify commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) and Non-Developmental Item (NDI) core maritime navigation software solutions that have the capability of being enhanced to meet USCG requirements (e.g. EAIS IDD). The primary objective is to survey industry capabilities to inform the prospective modernization and eventual replacement of the legacy USCG �Vega� navigation software suite (currently derived from commercial core navigation architectures) across the cutter and boat fleet. 1.2 Purpose & Scope of Market Inquiry The Coast Guard seeks insight into the current commercial and naval navigation software, including cutting-edge display engines, autonomous voyage planning, sensor fusion, resilient Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), and modern software architectures (e.g., modular open systems, containerized microservices, cross-platform runtimes). The Government intends to assess software suites that can match or exceed the complete operational baseline of current USCG E-NAV capabilities while remaining flexible, open, and capable of integrating seamlessly into existing USCG shipboard hardware configurations without requiring complete bridge refits. 1.3 Disclaimer This is a Request for Information (RFI) and is issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes. This is not a Request for Proposals or a Request for Quotations, and it is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract/order nor is the Government responsible for any costs incurred in furnishing information provided under this RFI. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this RFI or Government use of any information provided. Further, the Government is not seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals at this time. No classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response to this RFI. Proprietary information must be clearly marked if included. The Government reserves the right to use any information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate, including using technical information provided by respondents in any resultant solicitation. Responses will assist the Government in determining the availability of potential solutions and commercial products in the market. At this time, no solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the solicitation. The information and requirements in this RFI, and any attachments, is subject to change at the sole discretion of the Government. 2. Operational Environment & Hardware Baseline Constraints To ensure candidate software solutions can integrate into active cutter classes without widespread structural or electrical bridge overhauls, respondents must demonstrate compatibility with the following operational constraints: 2.1 Installed Hardware Baseline (E-NAV) The USCG fleet operates on a variety of IEC 60945 compliant hardware baselines consisting of: rack mounted industrial computers, rack mounted servers, ruggedized small factor computers, marine-grade All-in-One (AIO) Computer/Displays, system displays ranging from 15-19 inches, KVM matrix, ruggedized mouse and keyboard. 2.2 Operating System (OS) Gatekeeper Requirements Software architecture must natively support modern enterprise operating system standards: Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise (including Long-Term Servicing Channel [LTSC] builds). Enterprise Linux Distributions (e.g., Latest version of Red Hat Enterprise Linux [RHEL]). Vendors must state whether their software executes natively on Windows 11, Linux, or maintains a dual-OS cross-platform compiled codebase. 2.3 System Availability and Deterministic State Recovery Deterministic State Recovery: In the event of ungraceful bridge power interruption or system reset, the software must reboot and restore its previous operational state, active route, safety parameters, and sensor assignments without manual database rebuilding. 3. Core Functional Capability Matrix See Attachment. 3.1 Sensor Ingestion & Data Distribution Protocol Support: Native ingestion, parsing, translation, and broadcast of NMEA 0183, NMEA 2000 (IEC 61162-3), NMEA OneNet, and Lightweight Ethernet (LWE)(IEC 61162-450) protocols. Sensor Interfacing: Interfacing with gyrocompasses, Doppler velocity logs (DVL), magnetic compasses, wind sensors, depth sounders, GPS/DGPS/Galileo receivers, Inertial Navigation Systems (INS), and radar targets (ARPA). Integrity & Checksum: Cryptographic and checksum integrity verification for all data streams; automated detection and notification of malformed or invalid sentences. Decoupled Time Distribution: Network time distribution via UDP/TCP; ability to assign an authoritative UTC time source independent of the primary positioning source. 3.2 Data Recording, Playback, and Forensics Comprehensive Logging: Continuous background recording of ownship dynamics, sensor inputs, target tracking data, alert histories, and operator interactions. Storage Flexibility: Ability to write logs and telemetry to internal storage, external mission media (USB/NAS), or enterprise shipboard repositories. Visual Playback: Integrated forensic playback mode providing time-synchronized replay of chart presentation, radar overlay, and sensor states for accident investigation and tactical debrief. 3.3 Chart Management & Next-Gen Hydrographic Standards Legacy Format Support: Seamless handling of S-57 ENC, S-63 encrypted charts, and DNC (Digital Nautical Chart) formats. S-100 Transition Framework: Implementation roadmap and readiness for the IHO S-100 Universal Hydrographic Data Model, specifically: S-101 Electronic Navigational Charts (ENC) S-102 High-Resolution Bathymetric Surfaces S-104 Water Level Information S-111 Surface Currents S-124 Navigational Warnings Manual Corrections: Ability to create, save, import, and visually verify manual notice-to-mariners chart corrections and local marine hazards. 3.4 Operational Display Area (ODA) & Ownship Dynamics Ownship Dynamics: Multi-source position fixing utilizing GNSS (GGA/GNS), INS, Radar Chart Matching, manual visual/radar Lines of Position (LOPs), and Dead Reckoning (DR). Dynamic Calculations: Automated computation of real-time Set and Drift, Course Over Ground (COG), Speed Over Ground (SOG), Speed Through Water (STW), and Rate of Turn (ROT). Tactical Plotting: Rapid generation of Danger Bearings/Ranges, Clearing Lines, Variable Range Markers (VRM), Electronic Bearing Lines (EBL), and instant Man Overboard (MOB) emergency markers. RADAR Overlay: Software must be compatible with Furuno SDK and SSR COMRIC for RADAR overlay capability. 3.5 Human-System Interface (HSI) & Publications Visual Standards: Full conformance with IHO S-52 Presentation Library colors, symbology, and display modes (Day, Dusk, Night). Coordinate Precision: Coordinate calculation and display capabilities resolving latitude and longitude to one thousandth of a second (0.001�). Nautical Nomenclature: Standardization using Pub. 9 (Bowditch) and Chart No. 1 nautical symbology and abbreviations. Electronic Publications: Native viewer for hydrographic reference materials, Standard Bearing Books, and Adobe PDF navigation documentation. 3.6 Cybersecurity, Information Assurance & System Management DoD/DHS Compliance: Architecture capable of being hardened to DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs), meeting NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 security controls, and aligning with Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) parameters. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Distinct cryptographic user/administrator profiles, group policies, and role permissions preserved across software patches and upgrades. title: McMurdo PENGUIN Ground Station Antennas and Radomes
description: INTRODUCTION SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is issued for information and market research planning purposes; it does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is not seeking proposals at this time, but strictly the information requested, herein. Requests for a solicitation or proposals sent in response to this notice will not receive a response. Furthermore, those who respond to this SSN should not anticipate feedback with regards to its submission. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. The information provided in this SSN is subject to change and does not bind the Government to any future obligations. All submissions become the property of the Government and will not be returned. SUMMARY OF SCOPE The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS), under the Office of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Observations and the Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) / NOAA Antenna as a Service (NAaaS) program, is seeking industry capabilities and feedback regarding the procurement, fabrication, factory integration, testing, packaging, and sustainment of (5) receive-only satellite ground station systems for the PENGUIN Ground Stations project at McMurdo Station, Antarctica. See SOURCES SOUGHT 10-15-26 PENGUIN Ground Stations - Antenna Procurement Statement of Work FINAL for detailed scope of work information. PENGUIN Ground Station Overview Within NESDIS, the Office of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Observations maintains long-standing partnerships that support the acquisition, transport, processing, and distribution of environmental satellite data. These partnerships include cooperation with the European Organization for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites under the JPSS Program and are expected to expand to support the European Organization for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites (EUMETSAT) Polar System Second Generation (EPS-SG) constellation of microwave sounders. McMurdo Station, Antarctica, provides a strategic high-latitude location for polar-orbiting satellite data acquisition. At approximately 77.8 degrees south latitude, McMurdo enables frequent access to polar-orbiting satellites and supports Stored Mission Data downlink opportunities for NOAA and partner mission satellites. Additional receive-only ground station capability at McMurdo is required to maintain continuity, resiliency, and growth capability for NOAA environmental data acquisition architecture. The receive-only antenna and radome systems procured under this effort are expected to support known near-term mission needs, including EPS-Sterna L-band data acquisition at McMurdo. The Sterna L-band mission baseline includes Stored Mission Data (SMD) reception. The delivered antenna system is expected to include installed L-, S-, and X-band receive hardware capability. NOAA/NAaaS will establish S-band and X-band performance and interface specifications to support future mission requirements; these parameters are identified in the procurement technical specification. KEY ASSUMPTIONS AND RESPONSE INFORMATION Period of Performance: Base Period: 2 March 2027 � 1 March 2028 Option Period 1: 2 March 2028 � 1 March 2029 Locations: Performance of this work shall be conducted at the contractor�s facility. Delivery is expected to be made to the Government-designated logistics handoff point, currently Port Hueneme, California. NAICS and Size Standard: The Government contemplates the use of the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code: 334220- Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing, with the corresponding small business size standard of 1,250 employees. This is an open Sources Sought for all interested parties regardless of size, small businesses are encouraged to respond. The Government accepts recommendations for alternative NAICS codes. If a recommendation is provided, please provide the rationale for any code applicable to the planned acquisition other than the NAICS code identified above. Required Response Information: Interested Contractors are required to provide the following information in response to this Sources Sought Notice announcement: Company Name/Division, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, facsimile number, and website URL (if available). A single Point-of-Contact name, title, telephone number, and e-mail address. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code, Tax Identification Number (TIN), and company structure (Corporation, LLC, partnership, joint venture, etc.). Please note that companies must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be considered potential sources (https://www.sam.gov). Business Size (regardless of company size) and any socio-economic status, especially those qualified as one or more of the following: Small Business. 8(a) firm (must be certified by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA). Small Disadvantaged Business (must be certified by the SBA). Woman-Owned Small Business. Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business. HUBZone firm (must be certified by the (SBA). Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (must be listed in the VetBiz Vendor Information pages). A Capability Statement outlining why the respondent believes its firm has the capability to meet all these requirements outlined within SOURCES SOUGHT 10-15-26 PENGUIN Ground Stations - Antenna Procurement Statement of Work FINAL Relevant Past Performance Experience. Evidence of past performance of requirements similar in size, scope, and complexity. Conflict of Interest: Please detail the extent to which the respondent is aware of any potential organizational conflict of interest (actual or perceived) issues related to this requirement. Response Format: In order to better assist in the review of responses to this Sources Sough Notice, respondents are encouraged to prepare a capabilities statement that closely adheres to the following format: The document format shall be either Microsoft Word (.doc or .docx) format, or Adobe Acrobat (.pdf) format that is searchable. Responses shall be prepared using 12-point font, 1-inch margins, and 8.5-inch by 11-inch paper and shall not exceed fifteen (15) pages in length, including images, data displays, charts, graphs, and tables. SUBMISSION DEADLINE AND ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The responses received will assist the Government with identifying the number and nature of the entities that consider themselves feasible technical solution providers. Respondents are encouraged to ensure that their responses are complete and address all items outlined within this Sources Sought Notice. This Sources Sought Notice does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise, that a procurement action will be issued. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable government regulations. Any material received will be considered to be public domain unless clearly marked (on each page) as proprietary. The Government will not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for proprietary information not properly identified.
